Rosh Hashanah (Jewish New Year)

A Sweet New Year: Celebrating Rosh Hashanah at Home

Welcome the Jewish New Year with a day of reflection, tradition, and delicious foods that symbolize hope for a sweet and fruitful year ahead. This agenda guides you through meaningful customs from your own home.

  1. Morning

    Begin with Reflection

    Start your day with quiet contemplation on the year past and aspirations for the year to come. If you can't attend synagogue, consider listening to recordings of the shofar to connect with this central tradition.

  2. Late Morning

    Bake for a Sweet Year

    Prepare traditional round challah, symbolizing the cycle of the year, and a fragrant honey cake. The aroma will fill your home with warmth and anticipation for the festive meal.

    Recipes: Round Challah for Rosh Hashanah · Rosh Hashanah Honey Cake (Lekach)

  3. Afternoon

    Practice Tashlich

    Find a nearby body of flowing water – a river, stream, or even a large pond. Cast bread crumbs into the water, symbolically casting away misdeeds from the past year and embracing a fresh start.

  4. Late Afternoon

    Prepare Symbolic Foods

    Arrange your festive table. Slice apples and set out a bowl of honey, ready for the traditional dipping. Prepare pomegranates, symbolizing a year full of merits, for your meal.

    Recipes: Apples Dipped in Honey · Fresh Pomegranates for a Sweet New Year

  5. Evening

    Festive Rosh Hashanah Dinner

    Gather with loved ones for a special meal. Begin by dipping apples in honey for a sweet year, enjoy your round challah, and partake in pomegranates, wishing for a year as full of good deeds as the fruit is full of seeds.

    Recipes: Round Challah for Rosh Hashanah · Apples Dipped in Honey · Fresh Pomegranates for a Sweet New Year

  6. After Dinner

    Enjoy Sweet Endings

    Conclude your festive meal with a slice of homemade honey cake, a delicious reminder of the sweet year you hope to have.

    Recipes: Rosh Hashanah Honey Cake (Lekach)

May your home be filled with joy and your year be blessed with sweetness and good health.
